decision.summary: A minimal compressed perceptual runtime slice is viable only as an explicit opt-in layer for findings by dimension, gated by high-signal evidence and strict confidence handling.

current_runtime_boundary.current_behavior: Perceptual hints are passed only when explicitly enabled; hints are reading lenses, not target-brand facts.

rules: Compressed mode has no effect unless perceptual narrative mode is also enabled.
If high-signal detection fails, return baseline findings.
If confidence gating fails, return baseline findings.
If compression validation fails, production opt-in falls back to baseline.
Public report reads continue to prefer persisted narrative and must not trigger live LLM work.

safe_activation_conditions: target surface is findings by dimension only
run has enough evidence to support perceptual language
at least one direct or source-level evidence anchor exists for the dimension
evidence is not copy-only unless the finding explicitly remains copy-supported
generated text preserves at least one visible mechanism or source boundary
compressed finding does not introduce forbidden overreach patterns
output remains structurally compatible with Finding(title, observation, implication, typical_decision, evidence_urls)

minimum_rules: at least 2 evidence items in the dimension
or 1 evidence item plus a directly quoted concrete surface/detail
or repeated evidence from multiple source types across the run
preferred_rules: at least one quote or extracted detail

evidence contains surface mechanisms such as navigation, typography, image hierarchy, product objects, code content, templates, proof modules, service lists, reviews, screenshots, or source-stated interface details
the finding can name a signal before interpretation
fail_when: evidence is only generic marketing copy
the dimension only has score metadata
the signal would need to be imported from the perceptual registry rather than target evidence

high: repeated evidence across sections or URLs
medium: copy-supported reading with explicit source boundary
category-to-surface reading supported by concrete evidence

blocked_from_compression: trust, wellness, safety, therapeutic support, financial security, market leadership, or product efficacy without corroboration
motion or cinematic claims without capture, sequence, or source-stated motion evidence
weak, unverified, or human-review material unless limitation remains explicit

eligible_initially.reason: Useful for claim/signal gap, system consistency, proof structure.
Useful for surface visibility, attention hierarchy, channel evidence.
Useful for emotional temperature only when mechanism-bound.
Useful for category-to-surface translation and template behavior.

conditionally_eligible.condition: Only when direct evidence of motion, publishing rhythm, interaction, update cadence, or concept-bearing movement exists.

excluded_initially_when: evidence is copy-only and seeks to infer UX behavior
category is wellness, health, finance, legal, safety, or security and explicit caution cannot be preserved
finding depends on internal strategy, intent, audience sophistication, cultural authority, or leadership
finding would mainly add style vocabulary rather than evidence

fallback_behavior.condition: compressed mode is on but perceptual mode is off

fallback_behavior.fallback: baseline in production opt-in; raw perceptual only in lab comparison mode

reject_patterns: copy claim presented as product behavior
visual detail not present in target evidence
registry example treated as target-brand fact
preferred_suppression_output: or keep compressed finding only after replacing overreach with source-bound language
never silently assert a stronger claim

baseline_only: persisted public report reads unless an explicitly generated opt-in payload exists
sparse, copy-only, low-signal, or sensitive findings that cannot preserve caution
lab_only: raw perceptual output when compression fails
any run where human review is required before showing compressed prose
never_automatic: user emotion or therapeutic/support outcome claims
trust, safety, financial, legal, medical, or security claims
perceptual registry examples treated as target-brand facts
automatic replacement of baseline findings for all reports

rollout_boundaries.description: Explicit flag and paired baseline/perceptual/compressed outputs for reviewer comparison.
Compressed findings generated for selected high-signal runs and stored as experimental metadata.
Expose compressed findings only with baseline comparison and unsafe-overreach review.

monitoring_requirements: whether compressed text preserved evidence URLs
compressed better / baseline better / mixed / unsafe overreach
percentage of findings falling back to baseline
rollback_conditions: public reads trigger live LLM generation unexpectedly
compressed findings omit evidence boundaries for low-confidence material
sensitive categories generate unsupported user outcome claims
reviewer unsafe-overreach rate exceeds a small controlled threshold
fallback is not identical to baseline when gates fail
prompt output causes JSON parsing instability or report rendering errors
test_requirements_before_implementation: flag off produces baseline findings payload where feasible
compressed flag has no effect unless perceptual flag is also on
low-signal dimensions fall back to baseline
copy-only UX claims remain copy-supported or fall back
Visual Signature routes and outputs are unchanged
persisted public report reads do not call LLM
overreach terms are rejected or suppressed
final_recommendation: Prepare implementation only as an explicit opt-in lab-first slice. The runtime slice is viable, but only as a controlled editorial experiment, not a product default.
